body:
You are drafting short text for a dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd (D&D 5e, the valley of Barovia, ruled by the vampire Strahd). Reply in plain text only, no JSON, no markdown headings, and do not send messages to anyone else. Finish after one reply.

TASK A: ten journal entries. The game's quest journal is written in the party's own voice ("we"), past tense, plain and specific, one or two sentences, no more than about 40 words each. When a hero of the party is lost for good (they gave their life on the altar beneath Death House, or a card from the Deck of Many Things took them), their personal quest closes as a failure. Write the closing journal entry for each. Name the hero and the unfinished errand concretely; say they will not finish it. Do not say how they were lost (it differs), do not blame anyone, no lecture, one quiet specific image is welcome. Never invent new people or places beyond what is given.

The ten quests (hero, what they were trying to do):
1. A Seat at the Table: Ratatouille, a cook who learned magic so people would sit and eat with him; he wanted to apprentice to the Wizard of Wines and one day cook a proper supper for his friends and call himself a wizard.
2. Aurel's Last Chapter: Silvain Aster, a scholar, was looking for his colleague Aurel Mirescu, who went into the mists after a book written in a vampire's own hand.
3. Carry the Dawn: Liriel Dawnsong, a cleric of the Morninglord, was told in a vision to carry the dawn into this valley; she meant to sing real dawn into Castle Ravenloft's chapel.
4. Cold Prayers: Hedda Ironvow, a cleric, followed a dream of a dying sun and a silver raven; she meant to carry the raven's sun into the devil's chapel.
5. Grandda's Trail: Thistle, raised in the deep woods by the trapper Fen Burley, was following Fen's old trail blazes; Fen followed a great wolf into the fog years ago.
6. Count Off: Ilse Varga, a mercenary, was counting off her lost company, Kestrel Company, name by name, and meant to call the roll to the end in the castle.
7. The Fine Print: Kip Smudgewick, a halfling who signed a devil's contract (the devil is Mister Quillon) to save his family's apricot orchard; his way out needed a signature from the lord of this valley.
8. A Knight, More or Less: Godrick Pendlebrook was knighted on a deathbed with a soup ladle and carries his old master Sir Aldric's sword to be knighted properly.
9. The Last Lesson: Wren Featherfoot carried a sealed letter from his dead master Sorrel to Sorrel's old student Rahadin, Strahd's chamberlain.
10. The Woman in the Locket: Tamsin Tealeaf lifted a silver locket from a coach with no driver; the woman painted inside calls his name in dreams.

Style samples of existing journal endings (match this voice):
- "Kip called Mister Quillon to the fire and handed him Strahd's signature, and Mister Quillon read his own contract three times and went a colour Kip says he'll treasure."
- "Rahadin died before Wren could say Master Sorrel's name to his face. Whatever Sorrel meant his boy to learn at the end went into the ground with the chamberlain."
- "Fen asked Thistle to do it before the moon came, and she did, quickly, the way he taught her."

TASK B: Liriel and the Amber Temple. In the Amber Temple, sixteen sealed vestiges of dead dark gods offer "dark gifts" (power with a price). If Liriel herself accepts one, her quest Carry the Dawn fails: whatever she would carry into the chapel goes out in the amber. Write:
B1. One line Liriel says, as an interjection, the first time a vestige's voice speaks inside the party's heads. It must warn, in her own voice and fiction, that she will take nothing from them, because a light she bought from them would not be the dawn she was sent to carry. One or two sentences, at most 30 words.
B2. The journal entry when it happens (party voice, one or two sentences, at most 40 words): Liriel took a gift from the amber, and the dawn she was carrying went out.
B3. A short amber warning line for the journal while her quest is open (at most 14 words), in-fiction, not a game rule. Example of the form: "Nelu has been on that ledge three days already."

Liriel's voice: a gentle, devout elven priestess of the Morninglord, soft, clear, formal, a scriptural cadence she doesn't notice ("Be at peace." "The dawn comes." "Morning's grace."). Certain without being shrill. She never says Strahd's name lightly. Her secret: she is afraid of the dark. Sample lines:
- "Be at peace. Nobody should have to wait so long to be told they may stop."
- "Faith was always the thing I chose. Every morning, I chose it."
- "They answer, every one of them, the moment you speak. My god has been quiet all week."
- "Then we shall be quiet together, and buy nothing."

Format your reply as:
A1: ...
A2: ...
(through A10)
B1: ...
B2: ...
B3: ...
result:
A1: We lost Ratatouille before we ever found the Wizard of Wines, and he will never call himself a wizard now. His cast-iron pot is still strapped to the pack, waiting for a supper he will not cook for us.
A2: We went on without Silvain Aster, so he will never find Aurel Mirescu or the book written in a vampire's hand. Whatever Aurel walked into the mists to read will have to stay unread.
A3: Liriel Dawnsong is gone from us, and she will not sing the real dawn into Castle Ravenloft's chapel. The valley's morning looks no closer than it did when we came.
A4: We lost Hedda Ironvow on the road, and she will never carry the silver raven's sun into the devil's chapel. Her dream of a dying sun ends here with us.
A5: Thistle is gone, and she will not follow Fen Burley's old trail blazes any farther into the fog. If Fen and the great wolf left another mark in the deep woods, we will not know what it meant to her.
A6: We lost Ilse Varga before she could finish counting off Kestrel Company, and she will never call the roll to the end in the castle. We still have her folded list, with the last names left unmarked.
A7: Kip Smudgewick is gone, and he will never bring the lord's signature back to Mister Quillon to save his family's apricot orchard. The contract stays in his coat, every word of the fine print still binding.
A8: We lost Godrick Pendlebrook still carrying Sir Aldric's sword, and he will never be knighted properly. The soup ladle on a deathbed is the only knighthood he will ever have.
A9: Wren Featherfoot is gone from us, and he will never hand Master Sorrel's letter to Rahadin. We still have the wax seal unbroken, with no one left who knows why Sorrel wrote it.
A10: We lost Tamsin Tealeaf before he could find the woman painted inside the silver locket from the driverless coach. Her face is still shut inside the silver, and he will not hear her call his name again.
B1: Be still, and promise them nothing. A light I bought from this amber would not be the dawn I was sent to carry.
B2: Liriel Dawnsong laid her hand on the amber and took what it offered, and the dawn she was carrying for Castle Ravenloft's chapel went out right there in the cold.
B3: The things in the amber would gladly sell Liriel a darker fire.
